We developed a bio-inspired walking robot that is able to adapt to different environments and achieve complex behaviors by combining a biomechanics-based control system with distributed recurrent neural forward models with e-fference copies as sensory predictions. 1 Introduction The locomotive behaviors of animals are a result of the combination of biomechanical and neural mechanisms.

1) A combination of biomechanical and neural models can be used to generate complex behaviors in walking robots; 2) The neural mechanisms can be implemented using distributed recurrent networks with efference copy inputs; 3) The recurrent networks are capable of online state estimations and sensory predictions, and are more efficient than the adaptive neuron based models; 4) The combination of biomechanicals and neural mechanisms can generate complex walking behaviors in a robot, like walking on uneven terrains,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the neural mechanism of walking in biological organisms and how it could be used in artificial systems to generate adaptive locomotive behaviors.
the development of an autonomous walking robot with the ability to adapt its locomotion to different environments, and the underlying neural mechanisms for achieving such adaptation.
the study of the underlying neural mechanisms that allow animals to perform complex locomotor behaviors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel approach to online forward modeling with recurrent neural network based internal models for complex behaviors of walking robots.

the presented approach with adaptive internal model based on recurrent neural network allows the robot to perform complex behaviors as observed in walking insects, including walking along undulated terrains as well as climbing high obstacles.
we present a bio-inspired approach to walking robots that is able to perform complex locomotion tasks by integrating biomechanical and neural mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of recurrent neural networks as forward models in walking robots is a promising direction for achieving complex locomotive behaviors in walking robots that are comparable to that of walking animals.

the proposed approach can be a step towards building a more bio-realistic embodied system that combines the underlying neural mechanisms with biomechanical structures for achieving more complex behaviors.

the combination of biomechanical and neural mechanisms in the form of an adaptive internal model based control approach allows the robot to perform a variety of complex walking behaviors as seen in insects.
